message.content:
### Killing Visual Studio Code (`code.exe`) from the Windows command line

The simplest way to terminate all running VS Code windows (and any child processes it has spawned) is to use **`taskkill`**:

```bat
taskkill /IM code.exe /F /T
```

| Switch | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| `/IM`  | Kill by image name (process name). |
| `code.exe` | The executable that VS Code runs. |
| `/F`   | Force‑kill the process (no graceful shutdown). |
| `/T`   | Also terminate any child processes started by the target. |

> **Tip:** If you only want to kill the main VS Code window and leave extension hosts running, omit `/T`.

---

#### 1. Find the exact process name

Sometimes VS Code runs under a different name (e.g., `Code.exe` on older releases). Check the exact name with:

```bat
tasklist /FI "IMAGENAME eq code.exe"
```

or

```bat
tasklist /FI "IMAGENAME eq Code.exe"
```

If you see both, you can kill them all with:

```bat
taskkill /IM Code.exe /F /T
```

---

#### 2. Kill by Process ID (PID)

If you prefer to target a specific instance:

```bat
tasklist | findstr /i "code.exe"
```

Copy the PID from the output, then:

```bat
taskkill /PID <PID> /F
```

---

#### 3. Using PowerShell (alternative)

```powershell
Stop-Process -Name code -Force
```

or, to kill all instances:

```powershell
Get-Process code | Stop-Process -Force
```

---

#### 4. Batch file example

```bat
@echo off
echo Killing all VS Code instances...
taskkill /IM code.exe /F /T
echo Done.
```

Save as `kill-vscode.bat` and run it whenever you need to force‑close VS Code.

---

#### 5. Common pitfalls & notes

| Issue | Fix |
|-------|-----|
| **“Access is denied”** | Run the command prompt as Administrator. |
| **VS Code restarts automatically** | Some extensions or settings may auto‑restart. Disable “Auto‑reload” or close the window normally first. |
| **Multiple `code.exe` processes** | Use `/T` to kill child processes, or filter by username/window title if you only want to kill your own instance. |

---

### Quick reference

| Command | What it does |
|---------|--------------|
| `taskkill /IM code.exe /F /T` | Force‑kill all VS Code processes and their children. |
| `taskkill /PID <pid> /F` | Force‑kill a specific VS Code instance. |
| `Stop-Process -Name code -Force` | PowerShell equivalent. |

That’s all you need to shut down VS Code from the command line!
